newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc flies to new heights, others rally.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc flies to new heights, others rally.

text.p: Zinc galloped higher on Friday afternoon on waves of speculative buying, sweeping aluminium, copper and nickel with it.
"Once one metal gets going, the euphoria tends to spill over," said analyst Robin Bahr of broker Brandeis
Three months zinc touched a new seven-year peak of $1,625 per tonne, bringing gains over the past two days to $100 and the month's rise to $204 or 14 percent.
It ended the day $53 higher at $1,624.
The relentless rally has been fuelled by a battle between short Chinese smelters and long speculators.
The Chinese sold heavily short as much as 250,000 tonnes at low prices last year, analysts said.
Funds who expected a correction after prices hit $1,500 scrambled to cover short positions and have gone long, while delta hedging by option grantors has also fuelled the rise.
Option buyers have been snapping up both upside calls and downside puts, to profit from any further gains, but fearful that overcharged conditions may be building up for a breathless tumble.
Implied volatility surged as high as 32 percent on nearby options, up about seven points this week.
Analysts on Friday held out prospects that prices could sustain momentum to $1,700 and one said they may revisit $2,000, which prices last hit in March 1989.
The tightness, centred in September, forced the premium of cash over three months up about $20 to $60 at one point, ending the day at $55.
After zinc broke up through $1,600 in the afternoon, the U.S. funds piled into the other metals in a hectic LME session.
"They sensed that if they could get prices up to certain levels they could trigger short-covering," Bahr said, adding strong US economic data in the states may have also helped.
Aluminium also scored more upside gains, climbing $31 to a peak of $1,691, the highest since March 7.
The next target was the $1,701 high on March 4, which is also the peak for the year so far.
The key for the market would be whether producers decide to start selling heavily, Bahr said.

Technical tightness in August has supported the market, with the August/September spread trading at a $5 backwardation. At the kerb close the cash/threes was also tipping into backwardation, offered at a $5 backwardation.
Nickel charged up on furious short-covering, adding $405 in the space of a couple of hours to end at its high of $7,180.
Worries over contract talks which broke down at producer Falconbridge underpinned the rise. The current contract covering 1,400 workers at the Sudbury operation expires at the end of July.
Copper also joined in the fray, adding $82 to $2,374.
But once the short-covering was done, there was not a lot of scope for further gains as stocks keep growing, analysts said.
Tin added $80 to $5,390 but lead was the laggard, only managing to rise $7 to $653.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,500/$1,510, up from $1,480.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
